appraisal_events.evidence: « des regards chargés de mémoire, comme si elle avait eu peur et stupéfaction que mon amie ne se souvînt pas »; « l'autre, avec le même genre de discrétion qu'un homme qui voit son ancienne maîtresse avec un autre amant, cessa de la regarder »; « j'eus la preuve des goûts de cette jeune femme et aussi de la probabilité qu'elle avait connu Albertine autrefois ».
appraisal_events.explanation: Albertine is locally lowered by being written into Gomorrhe: the stranger's signalling is read as memory of past intimacy, and the ex-mistress simile casts Albertine as a former lover now dissembling. The narration corroborates only the stranger's tastes and stops at « probabilité » for Albertine, and frames the whole sequence as « mes préoccupations », so whether the text endorses the jealous construction is left genuinely open.

appraisal_events.evidence: « Je souffrais que mon amie vît qu'on faisait si attention à elle, je craignais que ces regards incessamment allumés n'eussent la signification conventionnelle d'un rendez-vous d'amour »; « Qui sait ? ce rendez-vous n'était peut-être pas le premier ».
appraisal_events.explanation: The narrator is diminished by his own account: his opening comparative judgment that the stranger is more beautiful than Albertine and that it would be wiser to give her up collapses at once into suffering, fear and surveillance, leaving him a helpless decipherer of signals exchanged over his head.

status_effects.explanation: She is locally tainted by the imputed Gomorrhan past, presented as probable rather than proven.
Her impassivity wins the exchange: « resta flegmatiquement immobile » makes the stranger withdraw entirely, and keeps her past opaque to the narrator, who gains nothing he can act on.
The passage is governed throughout by his jealous distress and exclusion from a past he can only reconstruct; no relief or intimacy follows.

ambiguities: The narrative stance toward the narrator's inference about Albertine is underdetermined: the text asserts the stranger's memory-laden gaze and the ex-mistress analogy as narration, yet hedges persistently (« peut-être », « Qui sait ? », « la probabilité »), and the confirming episode with la cousine de Bloch proves only the stranger's tastes, never Albertine's past.

The stranger with radiant eyes, her husband, and la cousine de Bloch drive much of the passage's action but are unnamed and absent from the reference sheet, so the evaluative movement they carry is recorded only through its effect on Albertine and the narrator; Bloch himself is named only as the cousin's relational anchor and is not a participant.
